claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §15: "The first digit of the status code defines the class of response. ... There are five values for the first digit" (1xx Informational, 2xx Successful, 3xx Redirection, 4xx Client Error, 5xx Server Error). §15.2: "The 1xx (Informational) class of status code indicates an interim response ... prior to completing the requested action and sending a final response."

RFC 9110 §15: "a client MUST understand the class of any status code, as indicated by the first digit, and treat an unrecognized status code as being equivalent to the x00 status code of that class." The lesson text ("must fall back to the first digit and treat it like the x00") matches; the ledger's "must not fail" is a paraphrase not used in the lesson.
RFC 9110 §15.3.1: "The 200 (OK) status code indicates that the request has succeeded. The content sent in a 200 response depends on the request method." Table: GET -> "the target resource".
RFC 9110 §15.3.2: "the request has been fulfilled and has resulted in one or more new resources being created."
RFC 9110 §15.3.5: "the server has successfully fulfilled the request and that there is no additional content to send in the response content."

RFC 9110 §15.4.2: 301 "the target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI"; "The server SHOULD generate a Location header field". §15.4.3: 302 "the target resource resides temporarily under a different URI"; "The server SHOULD generate a Location header field".

RFC 9110 §15.4.5: "the client, which made the request conditional, already has a valid representation; the server is therefore redirecting the client to make use of that stored representation"; "A 304 response is terminated by the end of the header section; it cannot contain content or trailers."

RFC 9110 §15.5.1: "the server cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error". §15.5.2: "the request has not been applied because it lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource." "no identity the server accepts" is a fair L1 paraphrase.

RFC 9110 §15.5.4: "the server understood the request but refuses to fulfill it". §15.5.5: "the origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource or is not willing to disclose that one exists". §15.5.10: "a conflict with the current state of the target resource".

RFC 9110 §15.6.1: "encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request". §15.6.3: "the server, while acting as a gateway or proxy, received an invalid response from an inbound server". §15.6.4: "currently unable to handle the request due to a temporary overload or scheduled maintenance".

RFC 9112 §4: "The reason-phrase element exists for the sole purpose of providing a textual description associated with the numeric status code"; "A client SHOULD ignore the reason-phrase content because it is not a reliable channel for information". RFC 9110 §15.1: phrases "are only recommendations".
RFC 9110 §15.5.4: "An origin server that wishes to \"hide\" the current existence of a forbidden target resource MAY instead respond with a status code of 404 (Not Found)."

RFC 9110 §15.5.4: "The client SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials. The client MAY repeat the request with new or different credentials. However, a request might be forbidden for reasons unrelated to the credentials." The RFC advises against repeating; it does not guarantee the answer "changes nothing". True of the lab's fixed Caddy rule, too strong as a general statement in section 6.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Actually `403` says the server understood the request and refuses it; repeating it with the same credentials should not be expected to change the answer.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution: outputs/stage-0/scripts/http/status-codes.txt at stage-0 lists 200 /index.html, 302 /redirect, 404 /api/v1/orders/999, 401 /admin, 409 /conflict, 503 /slow, 404 /no-such-page; the lesson output block is identical (diff clean). Caddyfile at stage-0 has the matching handlers (@missingOrder 404, /conflict 409, /slow 503; /no-such-page falls to file_server).

Caddyfile at stage-0: "handle /redirect { redir * /index.html 302 }"; captured output shows "HTTP/1.1 302 Found" and "Location: /index.html". Caddy redir docs: the target "Becomes the response's Location header."

Caddyfile at stage-0, handle /admin: "respond @guest ... 403", "respond @signedIn ... 200", "respond ... 401" with @guest = header Cookie *role=guest*. Captured output: "no cookie 401", "cookie role=guest 403".

Execution: the captured stage-0 run prints "200  /index.html" etc. from -w "%{http_code}  $path\n". Local run against an unreachable port printed "000  /a", i.e. the variable is the code of a response received, 000 when none was. curl is not in versions.yaml, so evidence is execution only.

Execution: captured stage-0 output for "curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null http://localhost:8080/redirect | grep ..." shows the status line and Location header on stdout and no body text, consistent with -D - (headers to stdout) and -o /dev/null (body discarded).
Source at stage-0, line 5: "[ -f /.dockerenv ] || exec ... lab-run.sh ..."; lab-run.sh ends with "exec docker compose exec -T lab bash -c ..." running the script inside the lab service.

RFC 9110 §15: the status code "describes the result of the request and the semantics of the response"; §15.3.1: 200 "indicates that the request has succeeded". Nothing in §15 derives the code from content; a 200 carrying a failure message contradicts that meaning.

Execution (bash, set -euo pipefail, loop of curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}  $p\n" against a closed port): printed "000  /a", then "curl: (7) Failed to connect", exit 7; second iteration never ran. So set -e stops at the first address, but the run still prints a number (000, curl's placeholder). If the lab is stopped with scripts/down.sh (docker compose down), line 5 hands off to "docker compose exec -T lab" and fails before curl runs.
claim_verdicts.source: local run 2026-09-26; examples/don-hang stage-0 scripts/lab-run.sh, scripts/down.sh
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: With only the site stopped, curl cannot connect: the loop prints `000  /index.html` (curl's placeholder, not a status code), curl reports the failed connection, and `set -euo pipefail` ends the run there. With the whole lab down, the script fails before curl runs.

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §15.6.3: 502 means "the server, while acting as a gateway or proxy, received an invalid response from an inbound server"; §15.6.4 defines 503 with no reference to an intermediary ("currently unable to handle the request"). The advice is conditioned ("When a proxy answers 502").

RFC 9110 §15.5.5 defines 404 as a response from "the origin server"; §15.6.4 note: "Some servers might simply refuse the connection." Execution: curl against a closed port gets no status line (exit 7, "Failed to connect").

RFC 9110 §15.5: 4xx "indicates that the client seems to have erred" and the server SHOULD explain "whether it is a temporary or permanent condition"; §15.5.5: 404 "does not indicate whether this lack of representation is temporary or permanent". The RFC does not say repeating an unchanged 4xx request usually fails; section 4 and the diagram state it as class meaning.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `4xx` the request itself seems to be at fault, so the fix usually starts on the client's side.

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §15.4 lists redirects "that indicate this resource might be available at a different URI, as provided by the Location header field, as in the status codes 301 (Moved Permanently), 302 (Found)"; §15.4.5: 304 redirects the client "to make use of that stored representation".

issues.quote: `curl` never gets an answer, reports the failed connection, and `set -euo pipefail` on the third line ... ends the run at the first address
issues.text: Not what this script prints. With only the site stopped, the loop prints `000  /index.html` before curl reports error 7 (reproduced locally), so a learner who tries it sees a number. With the lab stopped via scripts/down.sh, line 5 hands off to `docker compose exec -T lab` and fails before curl runs at all. Claim 21 rephrased.
issues.fix: Replace the mechanism sentence with claim 21 suggested_text; name how the site is switched off (e.g. `docker compose stop web`) and say `000` is curl's placeholder when no status line arrived, not a status code.

issues.quote: each method has a small set of codes it is expected to answer with, such as `201` for a POST
issues.text: Unlisted claim: not in the ledger. RFC 9110 §15.5 says 4xx codes "are applicable to any request method"; §9.3.3 only says a POST that created resources "SHOULD send a 201". "A small set of codes per method" is not how the RFC frames it, and 201 is conditional on creation.
issues.fix: Rewrite: "the other half of the exchange: the method you send shapes which codes make sense, such as `201` after a POST that created something." Add a claim citing RFC 9110 §9.3.3.

issues.quote: proxy — a program standing between the client and the real server
issues.text: Outline entry has `vocab: []`; tools/known-vocab --before this lesson returns none of proxy, gateway, status class, reason phrase, redirection, and `proxy` is not in content/glossary.yaml. Hard rule 2: terms outside known_vocab plus vocab.
issues.fix: Propose adding `proxy` (and the other Core-concepts terms if they are meant as glossary terms) to this entry's `vocab` in track.yaml via tools/merge-outline; otherwise remove the term from the lesson.

issues.quote: so sending the same thing again changes nothing
issues.text: RFC 9110 §15.5.4 says the client "SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials" and "a request might be forbidden for reasons unrelated to the credentials"; it does not promise the answer never changes. Claim 13 rephrased.
issues.fix: Use claim 13 suggested_text: "repeating it with the same credentials should not be expected to change the answer".

issues.quote: `4xx` the request itself seems to be at fault and repeating it unchanged usually will not help
issues.text: The retry half is an inference, not class meaning: RFC 9110 §15.5 asks 4xx explanations to say "whether it is a temporary or permanent condition" and §15.5.5 says a 404 may be temporary. Same wording in the diagram 4 branch. Claim 24 rephrased.
issues.fix: Use claim 24 suggested_text in section 4 and change the diagram label to "Your request seems to be at fault; the fix usually starts on your side".

issues.quote: Either the Location header names where to ask instead, or you already hold what you need
issues.text: "Either ... or" reads as exhaustive for 3xx, but RFC 9110 §15.4 also lists 300 (Multiple Choices), which offers a choice rather than one Location. Section 4 prose correctly hedges with "usually".
issues.fix: Change the node to "Not what you asked for. Usually the Location header names where to ask instead; a 304 says you already hold it".

issues.quote: reason phrase — the short text after the number on the response's first line, its status line
issues.text: Only HTTP/1.1 and earlier have a textual status line with a reason phrase (RFC 9112 §4); HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 carry the code alone. Claim 11 names HTTP/1.1, the lesson does not.
issues.fix: Add "in HTTP/1.1" to the definition: "the short text after the number on an HTTP/1.1 response's first line".

issues.quote: The `/admin` pair is the `401`/`403` distinction made visible
issues.text: RFC 9110 §15.5.2: "The server generating a 401 response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field". The lab /admin 401 (Caddyfile `respond "Unauthorized: ..." 401`) sends none, so the example is a non-conforming 401.
issues.fix: Preferred: propose (prompt 08) adding a `header WWW-Authenticate` challenge to the /admin 401 branch; no lesson change then. Otherwise add one clause: "a strict 401 also names how to authenticate, which this lab skips".
